Absolute-value borders in small MathI omit the extra bottom row. Large nested absolute/radical arguments keep a shared minimum bottom instead of adding a row per level; fraction arguments keep their measured extra descent.

Fixed reciprocal minus/one glyphs are supported in small MathI and align with tall bases. Postfix carets span the full fraction/mixed/parenthesis/absolute base with the proper bottom-row rule. Observed squares and reciprocals after all these bases, including inside an exponent.

PLUS exact surd evaluation now supports Abs. The sign of one/two surd terms is determined with exact rational squared-magnitude comparisons, without floating cancellation. Implicit multiplication before Abs is included; legacy 580 profiles stay unchanged.
Observed exact outputs: Abs(-sqrt(2))=sqrt(2), Abs(sqrt(3)-2)=2-sqrt(3), Abs(sqrt(2)-sqrt(3))=sqrt(3)-sqrt(2), 2Abs(-sqrt(2))=2sqrt(2), Abs(-1/2)=1/2, Abs(1/2)^2=1/4 and Abs(1/2)^(-1)=2.
All mathematical/format expectations above are native PLUS observations, not independently calculated replacements. Existing surd range and real numerical domain checks remain in use.
